question: A wire with resistance R is cut into seven equal parts. These parts are then connected in parallel. If the equivalent resistance of this new combination is R' , what is the value of the ratio R / R' ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**49**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **resistance** of a conductor is directly proportional to its **length** (**L**) and inversely proportional to its **area of cross-section** (**A**). The formula is given by **R = ρ(L/A)**, where **ρ** is the **resistivity** of the material.
 
• When a wire of total resistance **R** is cut into **7 equal parts**, the length of each part becomes **1/7th** of the original length. Since the material and area of cross-section remain the same, the resistance of each small part (let it be **r**) is **r = R / 7**.
 
• In a **parallel combination**, the reciprocal of the **equivalent resistance** (**R'**) is the sum of the reciprocals of the individual resistances. Since all **7 parts** are identical, the formula becomes **1/R' = 1/r + 1/r + 1/r + 1/r + 1/r + 1/r + 1/r**.
